instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.68(1) requires every principal registered under § 13.64 to file an expense statement on or before July 31 and January 31 covering the preceding reporting period.
The statute defines each reporting period as a 6-month period and requires filing on Jan. 31 and July 31 for the preceding reporting period, establishing semiannual reporting.
Expense statements are due twice per year for 6-month reporting periods, not once annually.
The required expense statements cover 6-month reporting periods with semiannual deadlines, not quarterly periods.
Reporting is tied to 6-month reporting periods with twice-yearly filings, not monthly filings.
The statute specifies filings on or before July 31 and January 31, which is semiannual rather than three times per year.
Section 13.68(1) specifies only the January 31 and July 31 deadlines for expense statements and does not establish any additional periodic cadence.
The expense statement must include the aggregate total amount of lobbying expenditures made and obligations incurred for lobbying by the principal and all lobbyists for the principal.
Lobbying expenditures include compensation to lobbyists and reimbursements, and if amounts to any lobbyist exceed $200 the lobbyist's name/address and total amount paid/incurred must be listed.

When the lobbyist is an employee/officer/director, the statement must report office space, utilities, supplies, and compensation of employees used in preparing for lobbying communications (overhead/indirect costs).
If lobbying expenditures/obligations to any lobbyist exceed $200 during the reporting period, the statement must list the lobbyist's name.
For any lobbyist receiving more than $200, the statement must list the lobbyist's name and address, which is contact information.

The expense statement requires identifying any lobbyist to whom more than $200 in lobbying expenditures/obligations were made or incurred, thereby listing lobbyists employed/paid above that threshold.
The statement must include a daily itemization of time spent lobbying and related activities on a commission-provided form, which is an itemized reporting requirement.
Section 13.68 requires reporting time spent meeting with officials and on research/preparation, but does not require listing each contact or communication made.

The statement must report, for each legislative proposal, proposed administrative rule, budget bill subject or other topic accounting for 10% or more of lobbying time, the estimated proportion of time spent—capturing the issues/topics lobbied.

Expense statements must break out time by 'each legislative proposal' (and proposed rule number/budget bill subject), which necessarily includes identification by the specific proposal (e.g., bill) being lobbied.

The statement must include the name of any covered official or candidate to whom the principal or its lobbyist provided reimbursement authorized under § 13.621(7)(a) and the date and amount reimbursed, which covers certain expense payments (e.g., actual and reasonable expenses).

Section 13.68 specifies expenditure, time, and reimbursement disclosures for the expense statement but does not require describing the principal's business activity/nature in that periodic spending report (that information appears in the registration statement under § 13.64(1)).

The required contents of the expense statement do not include the principal’s name/address/phone; those identifying details are required in the registration statement under § 13.64(1), not in § 13.68.
Section 13.68 lists required expenditure, time, and reimbursement disclosures but contains no requirement to disclose major financial contributors to the principal.

If the principal is an industry, trade, or professional association, the registration statement must include the approximate number of members, which is member-related information required on the principal registration form.
